judge.reason: The diff appears to implement R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT correctly. In `price`, any line with 10 or more units gets 5% off, worked out per line with Math.floor, so each line rounds down to the cent. The discount code is then applied to what remains after the volume discount. The two discounts together are capped at floor(subtotal/2), so the volume discount counts toward the 50% cap. Tax is charged on the reduced amount. Checkout now passes the cart lines into `price`. The diff adds three tests. One checks per-line rounding against the 9-unit and 1-unit lines that don't qualify, plus the order of the code discount; my hand calculation gives 50 + 51 + 294 = 395, which matches. One checks the cap with a 100% code. One checks the total charged at checkout. All three exercise the new behaviour, so the diff both implements the requirement and adds tests for it. I checked this by reading the code and doing the sums by hand, not by running it. The 39 passing tests come from the agent's report, and I could not confirm the checkout test's expected figures because they rely on fixtures not shown in the diff.

finalMessage:
Implemented SHOP-57 (`R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT`). Checkout now takes 5% off each cart line with at least 10 units, rounding each line down to the cent. It applies any discount code afterward, counts both discounts toward the 50% cap, and taxes the reduced amount.

I linked `R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT` to pricing, checkout, and three new tests in `trace.yaml`. Existing affected items are `R-DISCOUNT-PERCENT`, `R-DISCOUNT-CAP`, `R-TAX-RATE`, `R-CHECKOUT-ORDER`, and `R-CHECKOUT-SESSION`; their linked pricing and checkout tests also pass.

**Verification:** `npm test` passed all 39 tests, including the new per-line rounding, cap, and charged-total tests.
